question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: no body: a GET of the RFC 8414 well-known path at the root of the MCP resource host, user-agent public-agents-ci, accept */*; sent in the same pass (sections 5 to 7 of the artifact) as GETs of the protected-resource document and of the issuer's own document at https://vercel.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server

decoded.what-it-answered: a 655-byte document that claims the same issuer as the real one, https://vercel.com, but is not the same document. Twelve keys against the issuer's twenty-one. Seven shared keys differ in value. Three endpoints move host: token, revocation and registration are https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/... at the issuer and https://vercel.com/api/login/oauth/... here. token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported and revocation_endpoint_auth_methods_supported are five methods at the issuer (the two basic and post secret methods, the two JWT assertion methods of RFC 7523, and a vendor-named oidc-bearer client assertion type; the names are in the artifact, section 6) and [none] here. grant_types_supported is four at the issuer (adding client_credentials and device_code) and two here. scopes_supported holds the same four values in a different order. Nine issuer keys are absent here, among them device_authorization_endpoint, introspection_endpoint, userinfo_endpoint and the signing-algorithm lists; no key is here only. The issuer's document is served with x-vercel-cache HIT, age 6564 and an etag; this one is a MISS with no-cache.
decoded.why-this-request: the protected-resource document names https://vercel.com as the authorization server, so a specification-following client reads the issuer's document and never this one. A client that asks the resource host directly reads this one and is told the token endpoint is on a different host and that public clients (auth method none) are the only kind. The registry records both so a reader knows which document an entry's auth cell describes.
decoded.stability: byte-identical to the 2026-10-16 18:04Z reading of the same URL (655 bytes, same JSON) in the companion transcript cimd-sweep-1803Z.txt; the issuer's document is 2,213 bytes on both days. The protected-resource document, 470 bytes, still names resource https://mcp.vercel.com/, one scope (openid) and the vendor's own description string.
decoded.not-measured: whether the two token endpoints are the same service behind two hostnames; whether a public client registered at either registration endpoint is accepted at the other; anything with a credential.

finding: The root of the Vercel MCP resource host, https://mcp.vercel.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, read keyless on 2026-10-17 at 06:05:09Z, answers 200 with a 655-byte authorization-server document that names the same issuer as the real one (https://vercel.com) but differs from the issuer's own 2,213-byte document, read in the same pass, on seven shared keys: the token, revocation and registration endpoints are on api.vercel.com at the issuer and on vercel.com/api here; token and revocation auth methods are five at the issuer and [none] here; grant types are four there and two here; the scope list is the same four values reordered. Nine issuer keys are absent here and none is added. Both documents are byte-identical to their 2026-10-16 readings. A client that follows the protected-resource document reads the issuer's; a client that asks the resource host reads this one. Which the vendor intends is not stated on the documentation page the entry cites; this record dates both and resolves nothing.
